title: Auto Loans: Funding, First Payment, Payoff Quote and Lien Release Timelines
content:
Four clocks run on an Auto Loans account at Piedmont Crescent Bank: how long an approved application may wait to fund, how soon after funding the first installment must fall due, how long a payoff quote stays good, and how quickly the lien release goes out after a payoff.

## Timeline figures by product

| Loan product | Funding window (calendar days after application) | Latest first due date (calendar days after funding) | Payoff quote good for (calendar days) | Lien release sent within (business days after payoff) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Used Vehicle Loan | 30 | 45 | 10 | 10 |
| Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan | 30 | 45 | 10 | 10 |
| Auto Refinance Loan | 30 | 45 | 10 | 10 |
| Lease Buyout Loan | 45 | 45 | 10 | 10 |
| New Vehicle Loan | 30 | 45 | 10 | 10 |
| Green Vehicle Loan | 30 | 45 | 10 | 10 |

## What each clock measures

- The **funding window** is a span of calendar days measured from the application; an approved loan is expected to fund inside it.
- The **latest first due date** caps how far after funding the first installment may be scheduled, again in calendar days.
- A **payoff quote** remains valid for the stated number of calendar days, and the quoted figure grows by per-diem interest up to whichever payoff date inside that span the borrower uses.
- The **lien release** allowance is counted in business days, not calendar days.

## Distinguishing the products

The Lease Buyout Loan is the only product with a longer funding window, 45 days rather than 30. The other three clocks are uniform across the whole product line.
